anomalies.observed: The P-channel MOSFET Q3 is connected with its source pin (Q3.2) on the +5V rail and its drain pin (Q3.3) on the USB-C VBUS net NET0162. The LTC4412 ideal-diode controller U36 has VIN on NET0162 and SENSE on +5V.
anomalies.expected: For the stated LTC4412 + P-channel MOSFET USB input OR-ing/reverse-current-protection topology, the P-MOS body diode should point from the USB input toward +5V (source to USB VBUS, drain to +5V) so that reverse current from +5V back into USB-C is blocked when the MOSFET is off.

evidence.quote: LTC4412 controller and p-ch mosfet. need reverse current protection mostly

anomalies.impact: The MOSFET body diode is oriented from +5V toward USB-C VBUS, so +5V can backfeed into the USB-C connector even when the LTC4412 turns Q3 off. This defeats the intended USB reverse-current protection and may violate USB power-path behavior.

parsed.summary: The design files show a likely reversed P-channel MOSFET connection in the USB ideal-diode path: Q3 source is tied to +5V and drain to USB-C VBUS, so the body diode does not block reverse current as intended by the LTC4412 power-path circuit.
